name: adobe-commerce
_readme: Adobe Commerce (Magento 2) as source (Adobe Commerce Cloud, on-premise or self-hosted cloud; app/code modules over vendor/magento) and as target (Luma or headless on the Adobe Commerce GraphQL API, REST /V1 for integration, API Mesh / App Builder for off-platform extension). Seed from stable module-convention knowledge; no adapter.py yet, so the source role is documentation-only until one is written.

as_source.language_stack: PHP 8.x / Magento framework (Laminas + Symfony components), MySQL/MariaDB, OpenSearch/Elasticsearch, Redis, RabbitMQ, Varnish/Fastly
as_source.default_frontend: Luma theme (PHTML + Knockout.js, RequireJS, LESS); PWA Studio or a custom headless frontend on GraphQL as the alternative

snippets.version_markers: composer.json / composer.lock: magento/product-community-edition or magento/product-enterprise-edition (the 2.4.x line, and which edition - B2B and Staging only exist on Adobe Commerce), magento/module-* versions, magento/extension-b2b (or magento/module-company etc.) for the B2B suite, magento/magento-cloud-metapackage and ece-tools for the Cloud line; .magento.app.yaml (PHP version, mounts, crontab), .magento/services.yaml (MySQL/OpenSearch/Redis/RabbitMQ versions); app/etc/env.php (mode, cache backends); app/code/<Vendor>/<Module>/composer.json for each custom module. vendor/composer/installed.json is the only place with the versions actually installed - never derive a version from a module's own composer.json constraint.
snippets.active_units_config: AUTHORITATIVE = app/etc/config.php 'modules' array. A module that exists under app/code with a registration.php but is set to 0 (or is missing from the array) is DEAD unless another enabled module pulls it in - so compute the etc/module.xml <sequence> and composer require closure before calling anything dead. app/etc/env.php and, on Adobe Commerce Cloud, deploy-time environment variables (CONFIG__*, the Cloud UI variables) can override module state and configuration AFTER the repository - that layer is invisible to a code-only analysis, say so instead of asserting the effective state. Also check the AREA a module is wired for (etc/frontend, etc/adminhtml, etc/webapi_rest, etc/graphql) and the website/store-view scope of its config values in core_config_data: a module can be technically enabled and functionally inactive on the storefront.
snippets.package_sources: project composer.json require + composer.lock; vendor/composer/installed.json for effective versions; app/code/<Vendor>/<Module>/composer.json for in-tree modules (often without a version); patches declared through cweagans/composer-patches and magento/quality-patches in composer.json; m2-hotfixes/ (Adobe Commerce Cloud applies every patch in that folder at build time); Marketplace extensions arrive under vendor/<vendor>/ and are therefore NOT in app/code - a repository that only ships app/code hides part of the customization.
snippets.override_mechanisms: overridden = etc/di.xml <preference for="Magento\...\SomethingInterface" type="Vendor\...\Something"/> (replaces the implementation globally or per area), a plugin (before/around/after in <type name=...><plugin .../></type>), <type name=...><arguments> replacing a constructor argument or an entry of a composite/collection (the classic way core behaviour is swapped without a preference), a virtualType that rewires one consumer only, layout XML <referenceBlock remove="true"/> or a <block> class swap, a template/layout override inside a custom theme, and observers on core events. extended = a subclass or decorator registered as a NEW class or virtualType without taking over the interface. shadowed = a file under app/code/Magento/<Module>/... mirroring a vendor/magento path, or a class declared in the Magento\ namespace inside a custom module - both overlay core through the autoloader/generated code and are the highest-risk pattern. core-patch = an edit inside vendor/, a composer patch, or a file in m2-hotfixes/ - it is lost or conflicts at the next upgrade, count it separately. Interception limits worth naming: final, private and static methods and objects constructed before the object manager cannot be plugged; around-plugins on one method chain execute by sortOrder and a plugin that does not call $proceed silently disables the ones after it; generated interceptors live in generated/ and are stale until di:compile runs.
snippets.schema_sources: etc/db_schema.xml (declarative schema) together with etc/db_schema_whitelist.json - a <table> declared new is a new entity, a column or index added to a core table is an EXTENSION of a core entity (count the columns); legacy Setup/InstallSchema.php and Setup/UpgradeSchema.php in older modules; EAV attributes created in Setup/Patch/Data/*.php through EavSetup / CustomerSetup (product, category, customer, address attributes with their source, backend and frontend models - these are data, not schema, and they are the usual reason a 'simple attribute' is expensive to migrate); etc/extension_attributes.xml (extension attributes bolted onto core service-contract DTOs); etc/indexer.xml and etc/mview.xml (own indexers and the change-log triggers they install); etc/product_types.xml, etc/eav_attributes.xml, etc/product_options.xml for catalog-model changes.
snippets.workflow_sources: there is no BPM engine - name the mechanism instead: order lifecycle = the sales order state/status model plus status assignments written by data patches; message queues = etc/queue_publisher.xml, etc/queue_consumer.xml, etc/queue_topology.xml, etc/communication.xml (a consumer must be allowed to run, see cron/worker configuration); scheduled work = etc/crontab.xml (job groups and their configuration); async and bulk web API = the /async and /async/bulk routes generated from etc/webapi.xml; B2B approval logic = purchase-order rules configured as data (Magento PurchaseOrderRule), not code; Staging/scheduled updates wrap content, price and catalog-rule changes in campaigns and add a *_staging schema layer - a custom entity that must be schedulable has to opt into staging explicitly.
snippets.data_script_sources: Setup/Patch/Data/*.php data patches (idempotent, recorded in the patch_list table, ordered by getDependencies) and legacy Setup/InstallData.php / UpgradeData.php; config values written into core_config_data by patches - always read the SCOPE (default / website / store), a value written at default scope can be overridden per store view and, on Cloud, by deploy-time variables; CMS pages, CMS blocks and Page Builder markup embedded as HTML strings inside patches (grep for data-content-type to find Page Builder content created in code); CSV import profiles and import/export configuration; fixtures under Test/Fixture and dev/tests (intent only, never counted as production data).
snippets.read_order: registration.php + etc/module.xml (<sequence> = load order and hard dependencies) + composer.json, then etc/di.xml and the per-area di.xml files (etc/frontend, etc/adminhtml, etc/webapi_rest, etc/webapi_soap, etc/graphql), etc/db_schema.xml + db_schema_whitelist.json, etc/extension_attributes.xml, etc/webapi.xml + etc/schema.graphqls (what this module exposes to integrations and to a headless frontend), etc/events.xml, etc/crontab.xml, etc/queue*.xml, etc/acl.xml + etc/adminhtml/system.xml + etc/config.xml (admin surface and default configuration), view/frontend|adminhtml (layout, templates, web), Setup/Patch/**, then Api/ + Model/ + Controller/ + Observer/ + Plugin/ + Block/ + ViewModel/, i18n last. Only after that judge activation: app/etc/config.php, app/etc/env.php, the design/theme configuration and the store-view scope.
snippets.hosting_constraints: Adobe Commerce Cloud (Starter and Pro differ - always say which): the application file system is READ-ONLY at runtime, only pub/media, var and the mounts declared in .magento.app.yaml are writable, so file-drop interfaces, ad-hoc scripts and locally written caches must move to a mount, object storage or a queue; cron runs ONLY through the crontab in .magento.app.yaml (fixed set, minimum intervals, no arbitrary scheduler and no long-running daemon outside a declared worker); service versions (MySQL/MariaDB, OpenSearch/Elasticsearch, Redis, RabbitMQ) are fixed in .magento/services.yaml and no custom system package or PHP extension outside the supported list can be installed; Fastly is the CDN and VCL changes are only possible through the Fastly module's custom snippets, not by editing VCL; deployment is build/deploy/post-deploy hooks driven by ece-tools, with a maintenance window during deploy - no SSH build steps on production; outbound mail must go through an approved relay; node sizes are fixed, so a synchronous third-party call in the request path becomes the throughput ceiling; on-premise and self-hosted installations have NONE of these constraints - never carry a Cloud finding over to an on-premise target without saying so.

as_target.default_frontend: Luma theme (server-rendered) as shipped; headless on the GraphQL API with PWA Studio or the newer Edge Delivery Services storefront line

snippets.critic2_persona: senior solution architect who has delivered several Adobe Commerce (Magento 2) programmes, is an Adobe Certified Expert for Adobe Commerce architecture, and can tell core module from Marketplace extension and on-premise freedom from Adobe Commerce Cloud constraint
snippets.docs_domains: developer.adobe.com/commerce (module development, the REST /V1 and GraphQL web API references, PHP coding standards, extension points); experienceleague.adobe.com/docs/commerce-admin (business/admin behaviour, Page Builder, B2B) and experienceleague.adobe.com/docs/commerce-operations (release notes, upgrade and deprecation notes, the Cloud infrastructure guide, .magento.app.yaml and services.yaml reference); developer.adobe.com/commerce/pwa-studio for the headless reference storefront and its Page Builder renderers; developer.adobe.com/app-builder and the API Mesh documentation (developer.adobe.com/graphql-mesh-gateway) for off-platform extensions and API aggregation - App Builder actions and API Mesh are the sanctioned way to add logic without touching the monolith; github.com/magento/magento2 releases and github.com/magento/inventory for behaviour that is only visible in code. devdocs.magento.com is retired - its URLs redirect and must not be cited as a source.
snippets.best_practice: extend through di.xml plugins and constructor arguments, use a preference only when the whole implementation is genuinely replaced, and never edit vendor/ or carry untracked core patches (magento/quality-patches and declared composer patches are the only sanctioned route); express data-model changes as declarative schema (db_schema.xml + db_schema_whitelist.json) and data patches, never as Install/Upgrade scripts; cross-module access only through service contracts (Api/ interfaces and Api/Data DTOs) and extension attributes, never through another module's Model; keep the request path free of synchronous third-party calls - long-running and bulk work belongs in message-queue consumers and the async/bulk API; anything the storefront needs must be exposed in GraphQL (schema.graphqls + resolvers), not only in a controller or in /V1; a custom Page Builder content type is only complete with an admin form, a Luma renderer AND a renderer for the headless frontend in use.
snippets.critic2_focus: D1: version and deprecation facts - the exact 2.4.x line and its PHP/OpenSearch/Redis/RabbitMQ support matrix, module and API deprecations, which capabilities are Adobe Commerce only (B2B, Staging, Live Search, Product Recommendations) versus Magento Open Source, and Cloud versus on-premise differences. D2: is the claimed 'standard counterpart' really a core class or interface (name the module and the interface) or a Marketplace extension, and is the override mechanism the sanctioned one. D3: does the core plus the B2B module really cover the requirement in the target version and edition - name the module, and say whether the admin-side capability also exists on the API. D4: exact GraphQL query and mutation names and REST /V1 routes, whether the capability exists in GraphQL AT ALL (this is where B2B breaks down), and whether every needed Page Builder content type has a renderer in the chosen frontend.
snippets.expected_hotspots_d3: customer-specific and contract pricing beyond shared catalogs and tier prices; live ERP price and stock lookups against an indexed, fully page-cached storefront; punchout (OCI / cXML) which is not core; company structures deeper than one company with user roles (multi-level hierarchies, cost centres, budgets); quote workflows that deviate from the standard negotiable-quote state machine; requisition-list and order-template behaviour; multi-source inventory with an external WMS and reservation handling; document downloads (invoices, certificates, drawings) per customer; complex configurable/bundle/custom-option product logic and product relations; search merchandising beyond Live Search rules; consent, tax and data separation across websites and store views; installed-base or equipment data, for which there is no standard entity
snippets.expected_blockers_d4: on Adobe Commerce Cloud the application file system is read-only and cron is restricted to the .magento.app.yaml crontab, so file-based interfaces, custom schedulers and long-running daemons must be redesigned; core patches and vendor edits are lost or conflict at the next upgrade, which is the single largest hidden migration cost of a customized instance; GraphQL coverage gaps for B2B - negotiable quotes, requisition lists, company hierarchy, company credit and shared-catalog pricing are not as complete in GraphQL as on /V1 (verify per version), which forces either REST from a public frontend or a custom resolver layer; Page Builder content arrives as an HTML string with data-content-type markup, so every content type needs a renderer in a headless frontend and custom types need one written by hand; indexer mode plus full-page cache under customer-specific pricing and shared catalogs (cache-variation explosion, hole-punching, price index size); Fastly VCL only via the Fastly module; the website/store-view scope of every custom attribute and entity; message-queue consumers and async/bulk operations must be declared to run in the target hosting model; migration of EAV attributes, media and customer password hashes; the newer Edge Delivery Services storefront line has a different content model than Page Builder - decide which one the target is before estimating content work
snippets.content_model_notes: Content lives in CMS pages, CMS blocks, widgets, dynamic blocks and Page Builder. A Page Builder stage is persisted as HTML inside the page or block content field: every element carries data-content-type / data-element attributes plus inline styles, so it is markup and not a structured component tree. GraphQL therefore returns cmsPage.content and cmsBlocks.items.content as HTML strings. A Luma storefront renders every shipped content type out of the box; a headless frontend must parse that markup and provide a renderer per content type - PWA Studio ships renderers for the shipped types only *(verify the covered set for the target version)*. A custom content type needs a Page Builder configuration XML, an admin form (master format + preview), a Luma renderer and, separately, a renderer in the headless frontend - count all of them. Widgets and dynamic blocks are resolved server-side and are opaque to a headless client, and dynamic blocks depend on customer segments, which are an Adobe Commerce (not Open Source) feature. Adobe's newer storefront line uses Edge Delivery Services documents and blocks instead of Page Builder - the two content models are not interchangeable.
snippets.api_families_hint: see knowledge target_api_endpoint_families - two distinct surfaces: GraphQL (storefront, session-less, customer token) and REST /V1 (admin and integration, with searchCriteria and async/bulk variants); API Mesh aggregates them with third-party APIs, App Builder hosts logic that must not live in the monolith
